name: Europe hybrid attacks
summary: Estonia blames Russian military intelligence for a foiled 14 Nov arson at a drone maker; no casualties found
state: Estonia says Russian military intelligence ordered an attempted arson at drone maker Threod Systems on 14 Nov and will close its Russian border crossings from 1 Dec (CNBC, 16 Nov). Rzeczpospolita reported on 18 Nov that Russian intelligence planned, but did not carry out, a false-flag attack from Poland into Kaliningrad, which ISW assesses was likely deterred. No sabotage causing casualties or repeated multi-country airport shutdowns was found from 15 to 20 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Defence suppliers and critical infrastructure operators in Europe remain the main targets. In the UK, the NCSC and the NPSA publish guidance on protective security.
rubric_hit: Watch: sabotage incident attributed to a state (Estonia blames Russian military intelligence, 14 Nov); no casualties or multi-country shutdowns

why: Sabotage, arson and drone incursions over airports and bases are how state confrontation reaches daily life in the UK and Europe.
drivers: Russia–NATO tensions, drone and cyber capabilities, proxy recruitment, elections.

rubric.alert: Repeated airport or infrastructure shutdowns across several countries, or sabotage causing casualties or a major outage.
rubric.watch: Drone incursions close an airport or military base, or a sabotage incident is attributed to a state.
rubric.normal: No significant attributed sabotage or airspace incursions in Europe this week.
